backend.topology: single-node: 1 mon, 1 mgr, 1 bluestore OSD, 1 MDS; cephfs_data + cephfs_metadata pools; 1 client
backend.mount: ceph-fuse in the client container (the court kernel has no ceph.ko; /dev/fuse is present)
backend.osd_data: /mnt/1tb_kingston/WeftFS/.docker-cache/cephfs-20261114T162327Z/osd (host bind mount on the court filesystem, not a tmpfs; the receipt's non-claims still apply)

pool_settings.why: one OSD: size 2 is permanently degraded and doubles the bytes the single OSD must hold
pool_settings.why_session_timeout: a 4-CPU client running a 424 MB FUSE workload can pause between MDS messages; a blocklisted client wedges the mount

backend.label: SINGLE-NODE Ceph deployed in one OOM-protected container plus one client container on one host. Not multi-node, not a fleet, not clustered performance, not a cloud result. The OSD data directory is a host directory, so no media or power-loss claim is made.

server.why_capabilities: Ceph daemons run as uid/gid 167 and write keyrings they own

client.why_capabilities: ceph-fuse mounts through /dev/fuse; SYS_ADMIN is the minimum mount capability

arms.durability: every arm fsyncs a file and the directory, or publishes through the store's LocalBackend on the same mount; CephFS fsync orders against MDS/OSD

non_claims: single-node Ceph on one host, one client, one writer
no fleet, multi-node, clustered, cloud, media or power-loss claim
requests are client-visible I/O operations, not RADOS RPCs
the OSD data directory is a host directory, not a tmpfs
